chapter: Fisher's band and Jack Laine's bands
title: Fisher's brass band at Crescent Park and Gretna
summary: Fisher's real name was Phillips. Brunies led his brass band with one trumpet, playing at Crescent Park and Gretna, and could be heard far away; he then went with Shillen's band.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: His right name was Phillips, but they used to give him that name Fisher. Fisher. He's dead now. Well, it wasn't his real name. No, Phillips.

What sort of a band did he have? He had a brass band. And we used to play at the Crescent Park and Gretna. And they all used to use two and three trumpets for ten men or twelve men brass. I led the band with one trumpet by myself. They called me what they called the Iron Lick Conniprass. And we used to get on the levee in front of the park, and they used to hear me blow way back on St. Charles Avenue when we were playing music.
People told me when you played on Canal Street, they could hear you over and out.
So that went on, and so I went with Shillen's band. Shillen got a band.
